PROJECT CASE STUDY Page 2 of 4

Forged Carbon Fiber Motor Mount

ROLE: Mold design & layup lead TOOLS: SolidWorks, hand layup
Finished carbon fiber motor mount (top-down view)
57.9%
MASS REDUCTION
114 g (Aluminum) → 48 g (Carbon)

OBJECTIVE

Replace 114 g aluminum mounts with 48 g carbon fiber parts — a 57.9% mass reduction — without changing the motor bolt pattern.

DESIGN & APPROACH

Modeled a drop-in replacement in SolidWorks preserving the original motor bolt pattern, then designed a two-part aluminum mold. Hand-packed chopped carbon tow and resin into the mold, refining the layup through multiple iterations.

ITERATIVE MANUFACTURING

Resolved mold issues through testing: added draft angle to fix parts sticking, repositioned vents to address resin starvation, and adjusted clamping to reduce uneven flash.

OUTCOME

Finished mount weighed 48 g — a 57.9% reduction from the original 114 g aluminum part.

PROJECT CASE STUDY Page 4 of 4

Involute Gear Train

ROLE: Personal build TOOLS: SolidWorks (equation-driven), Prusa i3 MK3S, PLA
Involute gear train assembly isometric CAD
10:1
GEAR RATIO
3 reduction stages (smooth, no binding)

OBJECTIVE

Design and build a physical gear train with a 10:1 overall ratio across three reduction stages.

EQUATION-DRIVEN DESIGN

Built the involute tooth profile in SolidWorks using Equation Driven Curves and Global Variables so the gear geometry could be adjusted parametrically. Each gear ratio stage was defined by equations rather than fixed dimensions.

MANUFACTURING & CLEARANCE

Printed all gears on a Prusa i3 MK3S in PLA. Tested fit after each print and dialed in 0.15 mm clearances across stages to achieve smooth rotation without binding.

OUTCOME

Achieved a 10:1 overall gear ratio across three stages (12T→30T, 14T→28T, 14T→28T). The assembled train runs smoothly with no binding.
